at æde.explanation: "At æde" means "to eat" for animals: Løven æder kød (The lion eats meat). For people, use at spise (to eat): Jeg spiser frokost (I eat lunch). Said about a person, æde sounds rough, as if the person eats like an animal.

sentence.da: Hunden vil gerne **æde** kødet nu.
sentence.en: The dog would like to eat the meat now.

at ændre.explanation: "At ændre" means "to change" or "to alter", to make something different: Jeg ændrer planen (I am changing the plan). To swap one thing for another, use at skifte: Jeg skifter dæk (I change tires).

sentence.da: Vi må **ændre** planen, fordi det regner.
sentence.en: We have to change the plan because it is raining.

at ændre på.explanation: "At ændre på" means "to change something", to make part of it different: Vi ændrer på planen (We are changing the plan). To become different by itself, use at ændre sig (to change): Vejret ændrer sig (The weather is changing).

sentence.da: Han vil **ændre på** huset og bygge en altan.
sentence.en: He wants to change the house and build a balcony.

at ændre sig.explanation: "At ændre sig" means "to change" by itself: Byen ændrer sig hurtigt (The city changes fast). To change something, drop sig: Jeg ændrer planen (I change the plan).

sentence.da: Vejret vil **ændre sig** i morgen.
sentence.en: The weather will change tomorrow.

at ærgre sig.explanation: "At ærgre sig" means "to be annoyed" about something that went wrong, with a bit of disappointment: Jeg ærgrer mig over, at jeg kom for sent (I am annoyed that I was late). The little word changes with the person: Hun ærgrer sig (She is annoyed).

sentence.da: Hun vil **ærgre sig**, hvis hun glemmer billetten.
sentence.en: She will be annoyed if she forgets the ticket.

en æblekage.explanation: "En æblekage" means "an apple dessert", a classic Danish dessert of stewed apple, crumbs and whipped cream layered in a glass. Despite the word kage (cake), it is not baked as a cake.

sentence.da: Til dessert serverer vi **æblekage** med flødeskum.
sentence.en: For dessert we serve apple dessert with whipped cream.

en æbleskive.explanation: "En æbleskive" means "an æbleskive", a round, puffy Danish pancake. The name means "apple slice" (æble = apple, skive = slice).

sentence.da: Vi spiser en varm **æbleskive** med sukker og syltetøj.
sentence.en: We eat a warm æbleskive with sugar and jam.

en æggejagt.explanation: "En æggejagt" means "an egg hunt", a game where children search for eggs or sweets that adults have hidden, usually at Easter (påske), in the garden or park.

sentence.da: Børnene leder efter gemte æg i haven under en **æggejagt**.
sentence.en: The children look for hidden eggs in the garden during an egg hunt.

en æggemad.explanation: "En æggemad" means "an egg open sandwich", a slice of bread, usually rye, with sliced boiled egg on top.

sentence.da: Til frokost spiser jeg en **æggemad** med tomat og rejer.
sentence.en: For lunch, I eat an egg open sandwich with tomato and shrimp.

en ægtefælle.explanation: "En ægtefælle" means "a spouse", a husband or wife. Forms often ask for ægtefællens navn (your spouse's name), because the word fits both.

sentence.da: Din **ægtefælle** skal også skrive under på formularen.
sentence.en: Your spouse must also sign the form.

en ægtemand.explanation: "En ægtemand" means "a husband", a man in a marriage. In everyday speech, Danes often just say min mand (my husband).

sentence.da: Min **ægtemand** laver mad i aften.
sentence.en: My husband is cooking tonight.

en ælling.explanation: "En ælling" means "a duckling". Danes know it from the H.C. Andersen fairy tale Den grimme ælling (The Ugly Duckling).

sentence.da: En **ælling** er en lille and, som følger efter sin mor.
sentence.en: A duckling is a small duck that follows its mother.

en ændring.explanation: "En ændring" means "a change", when something becomes different. To swap one thing for another, say at skifte (to switch): at skifte sko (to change shoes).

sentence.da: Mødet er flyttet til fredag, så der er en **ændring** i planen.
sentence.en: The meeting has been moved to Friday, so there is a change in the plan.

en æske.explanation: "En æske" means "a box", usually a smaller one made of cardboard. A big box for packing is en kasse (a crate / large box).

sentence.da: Hun giver mig en **æske** chokolade.
sentence.en: She gives me a box of chocolates.

et æble.explanation: "Et æble" means "an apple", the round fruit that grows on trees. Danish joins words together: æblekage (apple cake) is æble plus kage (cake).

sentence.da: Et **æble** vokser på et træ.
sentence.en: An apple grows on a tree.

et æg.explanation: "Et æg" means "an egg". The letter æ sounds like the e in bed. Two common kinds are kogt æg (boiled egg) and spejlæg (fried egg).

sentence.da: Jeg koger et **æg** til morgenmad.
sentence.en: I boil an egg for breakfast.

et æggebæger.explanation: "Et æggebæger" means "an egg cup", the little cup that holds a boiled egg upright so you can eat it with a spoon. It is built from æg (egg) and bæger (cup). A bæger is a small cup without a handle, also in et yoghurtbæger (a yogurt cup).

sentence.da: Han sætter det kogte æg i et **æggebæger**.
sentence.en: He puts the boiled egg in an egg cup.

et ægtepar.explanation: "Et ægtepar" means "a married couple". For two people who are together but not married, use et kærestepar (a couple).

sentence.da: Det gamle **ægtepar** går tur hver dag.
sentence.en: The old married couple takes a walk every day.

et ægteskab.explanation: "Et ægteskab" means "a marriage", the lasting bond between two people who have said their vows. The ceremony itself is et bryllup (a wedding).

sentence.da: Deres **ægteskab** har holdt i tyve år.
sentence.en: Their marriage has lasted twenty years.

et ærinde.explanation: "Et ærinde" means "an errand", a short trip to do one small job, such as picking up food or mailing a letter. At a door or a desk, it also means your reason for being there: Hvad er dit ærinde? (What is your business here?)

sentence.da: Jeg har et **ærinde** i byen, så jeg kommer lidt senere.
sentence.en: I have an errand in town, so I will come a little later.

et ærme.explanation: "Et ærme" means "a sleeve", the part of a shirt or jacket that covers your arm.

sentence.da: Trøjen har et **ærme** til hver arm.
sentence.en: The sweater has a sleeve for each arm.

et æsel.explanation: "Et æsel" means "a donkey", a strong gray animal that carries loads. It is known for being stubborn: stædig som et æsel (stubborn as a donkey).

sentence.da: Et **æsel** har lange ører og kan bære tunge ting.
sentence.en: A donkey has long ears and can carry heavy things.

ædel.explanation: "Ædel" means "noble", for a good, generous character and for acts that show it. It also marks things of the highest quality: ædelsten (gem) and ædelmetal (precious metal).

sentence.da: Det var en **ædel** gerning at give sin plads til den gamle mand.
sentence.en: It was a noble deed to give your seat to the old man.

ædru.explanation: "Ædru" means "sober", not having had alcohol. It can also mean calm and sensible: en ædru vurdering (a sober assessment).

sentence.da: Han er **ædru**, fordi han ikke har drukket noget i dag.
sentence.en: He is sober because he has not drunk anything today.

ægte.explanation: "Ægte" means "genuine" or "real", for things and people that are what they claim to be.

sentence.da: Er den her taske af **ægte** læder?
sentence.en: Is this bag made of genuine leather?

ældgammel.explanation: "Ældgammel" means "ancient", much stronger than gammel (old). It is used for things that go very far back in time, such as buildings, customs and trees.

sentence.da: Kirken er en **ældgammel** bygning fra middelalderen.
sentence.en: The church is an ancient building from the Middle Ages.

ældre.explanation: "Ældre" means "older" or "elderly". It is the step up from gammel (old). De ældre (the elderly) is a polite way to name elderly people, softer than saying gamle (old people).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældre** end mig.
sentence.en: My brother is older than me.

ældst.explanation: "Ældst" means "oldest", the one in a group with the most years. It is the top form of ældre (older).

sentence.da: Min bror er **ældst** af os.
sentence.en: My brother is the oldest of us.

ære.explanation: "En ære" means "an honor", either a privilege you are given or the good name and pride that come from doing something worthy. Because it means the good name itself, it almost never has a plural.

forms.da: Det er en ære at møde dig
forms.en: It is an honor to meet you

sentence.da: Det er en **ære** at få en pris for sit arbejde.
sentence.en: It is an honor to get a prize for your work.

ærefuld.explanation: "Ærefuld" means "honorable" and describes a person or an action that deserves respect and has nothing to be ashamed of. It is built from ære (honor) and -fuld (full of), so it is "full of honor".

sentence.da: Han var en **ærefuld** mand, som altid holdt sit ord.
sentence.en: He was an honorable man who always kept his word.

æret.explanation: "Æret" means "honored" and is used for someone you want to show special respect. You mostly meet the plural form in speeches, where it opens the greeting: Ærede gæster! (Honored guests!)

sentence.da: Han blev budt velkommen som en **æret** gæst.
sentence.en: He was welcomed as an honored guest.

ærgerlig.explanation: "Ærgerlig" means "unfortunate" or "a shame", for a situation that goes wrong: Det er ærgerligt, at du ikke kan komme (It is a shame you cannot come).

sentence.da: Det var en **ærgerlig** misforståelse.
sentence.en: That was an unfortunate misunderstanding.

ærgerrig.explanation: "Ærgerrig" means "ambitious", wanting to achieve a lot and working hard for it. Do not mix it up with ærgerlig (annoying, a pity), which differs by one letter.

sentence.da: Hun er **ærgerrig** og vil blive chef inden for fem år.
sentence.en: She is ambitious and wants to become a boss within five years.

ærlig.explanation: "Ærlig" means "honest", saying what is true: Vær ærlig! (Be honest!). Ærligt talt (honestly) often starts a frank remark: Ærligt talt, jeg kan ikke lide det (Honestly, I do not like it).

sentence.da: Jeg vil gerne være **ærlig** over for dig.
sentence.en: I would like to be honest with you.

ærlighed.explanation: "Ærlighed" means "honesty", telling the truth and not cheating.

sentence.da: Jeg sætter pris på **ærlighed** hos mine venner.
sentence.en: I appreciate honesty in my friends.

ærter.explanation: "Ærter" means "peas", the small round green vegetables that grow in a pod.

sentence.da: Suppen har grønne **ærter**.
sentence.en: The soup has green peas.
